answer: Chained Attestation Ledger: each new agent identity must be co-signed by two existing agents, who record a link on a shared append-only ledger. Duplicating an identity forces the attacker to recruit distinct signers for every copy, so the signer graph grows like a terrace of redundant edges that auditors can prune. Colluding signers risk their own ledger standing, and each fake identity costs two independent signatures plus a persistent, traceable record. Anomalous fan-out surfaces at review time, much like footprints crossing a tundra or a canyon wall exposing layered strata.
